records.rationale: The equilibrium equations are useful, but the requested derived shape is left at a differential relation and the claim that nonzero-alpha solutions require numerical methods or series is too restrictive. An exact parametric quadrature follows directly.

evidence.finding: For H>0 and V(s)=w0*s+alpha*s²/2 measured from a horizontal-tangent point, dx/ds=H/sqrt(H²+V²) and dy/ds=V/sqrt(H²+V²). Their integrals provide an exact parametric quadrature, without requiring a cosh expression.
With V(s)=w0*s+alpha*s²/2, x(s)=x0+integral_0^s H/sqrt(H²+V(u)²) du and y(s)=y0+integral_0^s V(u)/sqrt(H²+V(u)²) du. Differentiating gives dy/dx=V/H and unit arc-length speed.
These integrals may need numerical evaluation for particular endpoints. The hold does not claim a generic elementary closed form or reject numerical methods.

records.rationale: The absolute claim that cross-multiplication assumes the desired equality and is necessarily circular is false. One may prove the cross-product equality independently and use reversible nonzero-denominator equivalence.

evidence.finding: A reversible equivalence can prove an identity backward from an independently established equality if denominators are nonzero. Cross-multiplication alone is not intrinsically circular.
For x!=±1, 1/(1+x)=(1-x)/(1-x²) follows from the independently verified identity 1-x²=(1-x)(1+x) and nonzero denominators.
An unqualified assume-and-manipulate argument can be circular; that risk does not make all cross-multiplication proofs invalid.

evidence.title: PROJ documentation, Mercator mathematical definition
evidence.finding: Official spherical Mercator inverse gives phi=atan(sinh psi), matching the real Gudermannian/NIST relation.
Identity, branch, domain and exact-value calculations are verified directly on the original domain.
Set t=tanh(x/2) and g=2atan(t). Then tan g=2t/(1-t²)=sinh x, sin g=2t/(1+t²)=tanh x, and sec g=(1+t²)/(1-t²)=cosh x.
For real x, g lies in (-pi/2,pi/2), fixing the real branches; the Mercator relation is the spherical normalized-coordinate version.

records.rationale: The rF*sin(theta) magnitude is correct, but rotation alone does not make that force angle equal omega*t or torque sinusoidal. The answer also incorrectly presents sinusoidal torque as the reason for the generator emf waveform.

evidence.title: OpenStax Physics, Motors, Generators, and Transformers
evidence.finding: For a loop rotating at constant speed in a uniform magnetic field, induced emf follows the changing magnetic flux and equals NAB*omega*sin(omega*t). Torque is a separate r cross F quantity.
Identity, branch, domain and exact-value calculations are verified directly on the original domain.

A tangential driving force has theta=pi/2 and constant rF torque during rotation. For an ideal rotating resistively loaded coil, emf=C sin(omega*t), current=emf/R, and electromagnetic torque magnitude emf*current/omega is proportional to sin²(omega*t), not sin(omega*t).
Sinusoidal emf in the standard generator follows the flux derivative under uniform-field, constant-speed geometry; load torque depends on current and operating conditions.
